As I was taking a stroll through the park, I found myself thinking and couldn't help but recognize the similarities:

  • Both provide entertainment
  • Both have a price, one is fixed, for the other you never stop paying
  • Both will ask lot of micro-transactions nowadays to enjoy all of the content
  • Both have a modding community
  • Playing them for long periods of time will give you headaches, it's not healthy
  • A lot of them focus only on shallow multiplayer modes that pander to the biggest possible audience to maximize income (Call of duty and similar)
  • The few that deliver a solid, enjoyable single-player experience with nice writing, graphics and atmosphere are the best (Metro 2033)
  • Few age really well. Those that have the style, taste and design to age well remain playable forever (Fallout 1/2).
  • Most have issues with roots in the development phase, issues that drag on to remain unsolved after publishing.
  • Most have sequels which carry on to have the same issues or perpetuate the same shallow concept
  • Most are focused on graphics these days, while sacrificing writing and gameplay.
  • Those that were part of your childhoold/adolescence tend to be very memorable, for better or worse.
  • Some are dumb but can be enjoyable (Mass Effect, Bioware games in general)
  • Some will tell you enjoyable tales, other can be loudmouths and condescendingly prattle their agenda
  • Some take time to get used to and to know, but are beautiful and rewarding if you put in the effort (The Witcher), you never forget those.
  • Some are smart, but cold and frigid (Europa Universalis and similar)
  • Some are just bat-shit insane (Killer 7, No More Heroes)
  • Some can be incredibly cute, yet serious (Cave Story
  • Some will try to keep you on edge all the time and take your management skills to the limit (Starcraft, RTS)
  • Some can be scary, but fun. (Resident Evil 4)
  • Some are just straight up scary nightmare fuel and you don't know why you keep playing (Outlast)
  • Some are like MMOs, nothing but grindy, empty content with no real satisfaction or deepness to be found.
  • Some are bubbly and happy, you can't help but feel at ease (Mario Galaxy)

There's no doubt more parallels to be found, but I will leave it there.
